findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: There wasn’t a Certified Food Protection Manager present at the start of the inspection. The individual that holds a food manager certificate arrived in the midst of the inspection. Discussed with person in charge (PIC) that a CFPM is required to be on site at all times if preparing and serving food. Ensure that there are more employees that are food manager certified to cover all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: The facility could not produce any employee health reporting forms. A copy of an employee health form was given to the manager for employees to sign and complete. The employee working at the time of the inspection signed the form during the visit. Ensure that all employees sign employee health forms and be sure that they’re conveniently located for future inspections.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Two containers of waffle batter were observed at room temperature in the service area. The employees planned to keep the leftover batter from breakfast, however, instructions on the waffle mix stated that batter must either be used within 4 hours or discarded (if not cold held during service) or kept at 41F or below at all times. Discussed with the employees that if there are plans to keep the batter for another day of service, the batter must stay cold held at 41F or below. If batter remains at room temperature, then the batter will need to be discarded after 4 hours. The batter was voluntarily discarded by the facility to correct the violation. Be sure to follow the manufacturer's instructions regarding Time/Temperature control foods to ensure safety of food items.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: There was a container of cream cheese spreads observed at room temperature in the service station. The packaging stated to keep items refrigerated. PIC mentioned that the containers are normally placed in the freezer overnight and are expected to keep the spreads cold through breakfast hours. Suggested switching out containers half way through breakfast to ensure that the spreads are maintaining proper cold holding temperatures. Ensure that TCS foods are cold held at 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed 2 gallons of 2% milk to exceed the manufacturer’s use-by-date. The dates were 1/22/2025 and 1/29/2025. Discussed with PIC and milks were discarded. Ensure that gallons of milks are date marked and never exceed the manufacturer’s use-by-date.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: The facility could not locate a temperature measuring device for the heat sanitizing dish machine. The inspector provided the PIC with a couple thermo stickers to test the machine. Ensure that a temperature measuring device is available to accurately measure heat sanitizing temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.115 Warewashing Machines, Temperature Measuring Devices. A WAREWASHING machine shall be equipped with a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE that indicates the temperature of the water: (A) In each wash and rinse tank; and (B) As the water enters the hot water SANITIZING final rinse manifold or in the chemical SANITIZING solution tank.
